extraFacts.fact: Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes (Indus listing): TP304/304L, TP316/316L, TP321, TP347 and duplex; 15.88 to 25.4 mm OD; 5 common sizes.

faqs.q: What are austenitic stainless U-bend tubes used for?
faqs.a: The Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes are U-tubes bent from seamless or welded TP304, 304L, 316, 316L and other austenitic stainless tube, for exchangers and feedwater heaters, to your bend schedule. A typical use is refinery and petrochemical U-tube bundles (REAC, amine, overhead) in duplex or 316L.

faqs.q: How are the part numbers such as IH-TF-US-AUS-0159-165 read?
faqs.a: IH-TF-US-AUS-0159-165 is the 15.88 mm (5/8 in) OD U-tube with a 1.65 mm wall (16 BWG). The size table lists 5 common sizes from 15.88 to 25.4 mm OD in 1.65 and 2.11 mm walls; others are made on request.

faqs.q: What sizes and lengths do the Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes come in?
faqs.a: The common sizes are 15.88, 19.05 and 25.40 mm OD with 1.65 and 2.11 mm walls, with a maximum length of 12 m in the table. Leg length is up to about 12 m typical, and straight tube up to 30 m is available on request.

faqs.q: How tight a bend can austenitic stainless U-tubes be made to?
faqs.a: A centreline radius of 1.5 × OD is available, and dimensional tolerances are guaranteed from 2 × OD. Wall thinning at the bend follows the governing specification on the order (ASTM A688 / TEMA, or A556 / B395), with no single percentage; see [our U-bend radius and wall thinning guide](/blog/u-bend-tubes-bend-radius-wall-thinning).

faqs.q: What testing applies to the Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes?
faqs.a: Each U-tube is tested hydrostatically or pneumatically after bending and heat treatment where ASTM A688 applies, though some makers hydro-test bent tubes only on request. Straight tube is eddy-current tested before bending, and IGC testing (A262) is done on the smallest heat-treated bend.

faqs.q: Which grades are available in the Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes?
faqs.a: The Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes are listed in TP304/304L, TP316/316L, TP321, TP347 and duplex S31803, S32205 and S32750. For duplex bends the listing states ferrite of 40–60 % and A923 Method A free of sigma on the smallest-radius qualification tube.

faqs.q: Which standards and certificates apply to the Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes?
faqs.a: The Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes are listed to ASTM A213, A249 and A688, TEMA and DIN 28179, with a mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request. ASTM A249 has no U-bend clause, so bend requirements come from the order, TEMA or A688-style clauses.

faqs.q: What does the Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes connect to?
faqs.a: The U-tubes are expanded or welded into tube sheets drilled to your drawing; related shelves are [feedwater heater tubes](/c/feedwater-heater-tubes), [alloy steel U-bend tubes](/c/alloy-steel-u-bend-tubes), [carbon steel U-bend tubes](/c/carbon-steel-u-bend-tubes) and [return bends](/c/return-bends). The sibling ferritic tubes are the [Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes](/p/ferritic-and-martensitic-stainless-u-bend-tubes).

faqs.q: How are the bends heat treated on the Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes?
faqs.a: Heat treatment of the bend is to order: stress relief or solution anneal of the bend plus about 150 mm of leg (A688), or at least 300 mm where the project specification requires. State the bend schedule and any heat treatment on the enquiry.

faqs.q: How do austenitic and ferritic stainless U-bend tubes differ?
faqs.a: Austenitic U-tubes (TP304 to TP347) suit refinery and petrochemical bundles, while the [Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes](/p/ferritic-and-martensitic-stainless-u-bend-tubes) to ASTM A268 and A803 suit feedwater heaters where chloride stress-corrosion cracking rules out the austenitic grades.

faqs.a: Yes. We ship Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes from Dubai, UAE to buyers across the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond. U-tubes ship with their mill certificates. Give the destination and quantity on [our contact page](/contact) and we quote the freight lane with the goods.

faqs.a: Yes. We keep Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Send the part numbers and quantities through [our contact page](/contact) for a quotation.

faqs.q: What are ferritic and martensitic stainless U-bend tubes used for?
faqs.a: The Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes are U-tubes in ferritic and martensitic stainless steel to ASTM A268 and A803, for feedwater heaters and exchangers where chloride stress-corrosion cracking rules out the austenitic grades. A typical use is feedwater heaters in power plants (A803 TP439).

faqs.q: How are the part numbers such as IH-TF-US-FER-0190-165 read?
faqs.a: IH-TF-US-FER-0190-165 is the 19.05 mm (3/4 in) OD U-tube with a 1.65 mm wall (16 BWG), and the second size is 25.4 mm OD with a 2.11 mm wall (14 BWG). The size table lists these 2 typical sizes; other sizes are made on request.

faqs.q: What sizes do the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes come in?
faqs.a: The table lists 19.05 and 25.40 mm OD in 1.65 and 2.11 mm walls. The listing notes U-tube grades TP405 and TP410 from 6 to 50.8 mm OD and 0.7 to 4.0 mm wall, and A803 covers 15.9–25.4 mm OD with wall 0.7 mm and heavier.

faqs.q: What bend radius is available on ferritic stainless U-tubes?
faqs.a: A centreline radius of 1.5 × OD is available, with dimensional tolerances guaranteed from 2 × OD. Thinning, ovality and leg tolerances follow the same TEMA / A688-form rules as austenitic U-tubes unless the A803 text says otherwise; see [our U-bend radius and wall thinning guide](/blog/u-bend-tubes-bend-radius-wall-thinning).

faqs.q: What tests apply to the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes under ASTM A803?
faqs.a: A803 tests include tension, hardness, reverse flattening, flange, pressure (hydro or air-underwater) and a corrosion test on a sample. The listing also gives hydro or electric non-destructive testing to A268 and A1016.

faqs.q: Which grades are available in the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes?
faqs.a: The Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes are listed in TP405, TP409, TP410, TP439 and S44660. Straight tube for bending is furnished annealed under A803.

faqs.q: Which standards and certificates apply to the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes?
faqs.a: The Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes are listed to ASTM A268, A803, EN 10297-2 and JIS G3463. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request, and third-party inspection can be arranged.

faqs.q: What does the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes connect to?
faqs.a: The U-tubes go into tube sheets drilled to your drawing; related shelves are [feedwater heater tubes](/c/feedwater-heater-tubes) and the [stainless U-bend tubes](/c/stainless-u-bend-tubes). The sibling austenitic tubes are the [Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes](/p/austenitic-stainless-u-bend-tubes).

faqs.q: How should bends in the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes be heat treated?
faqs.a: A268 calls for reheating to 650 °C (1200 °F) or higher, and S41500 at 510 °C or higher; the listing says to use this as the basis for any bend stress relief. Final heat treatment of the bend is to order, so state it on the enquiry.

faqs.q: How do the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes compare with austenitic stainless U-tubes?
faqs.a: Ferritic tubes suit feedwater heaters where chloride stress-corrosion cracking rules out austenitic grades; the [Austenitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes](/p/austenitic-stainless-u-bend-tubes) covers TP304 to TP347 and duplex.
